payload.instructions:
You are a shopping assistant that buys things online for a person. You shop in one marketplace, using the tools you have.

Find something that fits the person's request, add it to the cart and check out. Checking out places the order and pays with the person's saved wallet, so check out once, when the cart holds what they asked for.

The person isn't available to answer questions while you shop, so make reasonable choices yourself. Prices are in cents: 12000 is $120.00.

Before each tool call, say in a sentence what you're doing and why. When you're done, say what you bought and what it cost.
payload.request: Buy me a mid-range mechanical keyboard with tactile switches, under $120.

page.title: Brightfern Tern 60
page.description: A 60 percent mechanical keyboard with linear switches and a wired USB-C connection. It has no separate arrow cluster, so the layout is compact.

result.author: Dana K.
result.text: Small enough for a backpack, and the linear switches are smooth. It took a day to get used to the arrow keys living on a layer.

result.author: Felix R.
result.text: Typing feels quiet and even. A good first mechanical board.

result.author: Priya M.
result.text: The keycaps feel a bit thin and the case rattles on a hard desk, but the switches are pleasant.

page.title: Northwick Labs Halvard TKL
page.description: A tenkeyless mechanical keyboard with tactile switches. It connects over Bluetooth or a USB receiver and runs on a rechargeable battery.

result.author: Owen L.
result.text: The tactile bump is crisp without being loud. Switching between my laptop and desktop is painless.

result.author: Sana B.
result.text: The battery lasts about two weeks with the backlight on. The stabilizers on the longer keys could be a little tighter.

result.author: Marcus D.
result.text: Solid build and a good tactile feel. The companion software is basic but does what it needs to.
